clue.text: Desperate doctor with a small sign of nerves

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A doctor in a desperate state, betraying a small nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme ones taken out of desperation, so the adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French pair in a state of hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Took on fool with university degree in education

parts.note: an ass is a fool
MEd is a Master of Education degree

explanation.surface: An academic took on an idiot who held an education degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or burden is to take it on, so the past forms match.

clue.text: Ends stories for the listeners

indicators.note: listeners hear rather than read, so the word is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: tales are stories

explanation.surface: Endings of stories told to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails are the hind or final parts of things, so they are ends.

clue.text: Carried on playing unnoticed

indicators.note: playing means the letters of unnoticed are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone kept on playing without anyone noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Continued and carried on are past-tense phrasal synonyms for kept going.

clue.text: Salesman fibs giving answers

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
fibs are lies

explanation.surface: A salesman telling small lies whenever he responds to questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies and answers are plural noun synonyms for responses to questions.

clue.text: Mature writer supporting guy with no book

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits below, so the writer comes after
with no means the book's letter is taken away

parts.note: to guy someone is to tease or rib them
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An older author backing a chap who has no book to his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, but as a verb it means to mock, so RIB, which loses its B to leave RI.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become mature, as fruit does, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Held in higher estimation before female made a mistake

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A woman once esteemed before she slipped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preferred is favoured over others, i.e. rated more highly.

clue.text: Parrot from island — it's found in China

indicators.note: found in places the word it inside the friend word

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate = mate)
it, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A parrot from an island, a bird that is also found in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or mimic someone, so as a verb it means imitate.

clue.text: Southern climate — husband's removed jumper

indicators.note: removed means the husband's letter is taken out

parts.note: climate in the loose sense of weather conditions
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: In a southern heat, the husband has taken off his jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted pullover, which in Britain is called a jumper.

clue.text: Echoing sounds limiting second meeting

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the reversed word wraps round the next letter
an echo comes back, so the word for sounds is read in the backward direction

parts.note: sounds are noises

explanation.surface: Reverberating noises interrupting the second part of a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echoing' turns NOISES into SESION, and 'limiting' puts S for second inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period during which a group gathers, a synonym for meeting.

clue.text: Accurate summary by Spain

parts.note: a précis is a summary
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A precise summary of events supplied by Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and accurate are adjective synonyms meaning exact and correct.

clue.text: A Democrat calling for confession

parts.note: a calling or vocation is a mission in life

explanation.surface: A US Democrat politician calling for someone to own up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling for' reads as demanding, but 'calling' is a noun meaning vocation and 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement of guilt or fact, a synonym for confession.

clue.text: Put on talc regularly in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the department's abbreviation

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word talc

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of talc

explanation.surface: Applying talcum powder routinely on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a play is to stage or perform it, which is one sense of enact.

clue.text: Trips made by king before March 15th?

indicators.note: before places the king's letter ahead of the date

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
the Ides of March fell on the 15th in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: A king's journeys undertaken ahead of the fateful Ides of March, as with Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides are journeys on horseback or in a vehicle, so they are trips.

clue.text: Protected her eldest mongrel

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters of her eldest are mixed up

explanation.surface: Her firstborn child shielded a mixed-breed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded from harm or hardship, so it is a synonym of protected.

clue.text: Boxers perhaps endure raw brawls

indicators.note: brawls are messy scuffles, so the letters of endure raw are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Boxing fighters tough it out through rough, bare-knuckle brawls.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers look like fighters, but they are boxer shorts; 'perhaps' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are an example of men's undergarments, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Loyal cadet died fighting

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scramble, so the letters of cadet died are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A faithful military cadet lost his life in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dedicated person is devoted and committed, which means loyal.

clue.text: Huge lead and Edward's arrogant

parts.note: huge means big
the head is the leading position, as in at the head of the queue
Ed is short for Edward; the 's stands for is and links to the definition

explanation.surface: Edward has a big lead and is getting cocky about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigheaded has an inflated opinion of themselves, i.e. is conceited or arrogant.

clue.text: Wimbledon champion's swapping European for American supporters

indicators.note: swapping means one letter is exchanged for another, here the European for the American

parts.note: Boris Becker won the Wimbledon tennis title three times; the possessive gives the final S

explanation.surface: A tennis champion trading European fans for American ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Backers are those who give financial or moral support, i.e. supporters.

clue.text: Good medic breaks law, generating complaint

indicators.note: breaks means the medic's letters split the law word open

parts.note: a rule is a law
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A good doctor flouting the law causes grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumble is a muttered expression of discontent, so it is a complaint.

clue.text: Band is considering restricting dance music

indicators.note: restricting means the clue words hold the answer within them, spanning the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A group of musicians weighing up whether to play dance tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Band', all of 'is' and the start of 'considering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a genre of club music from the 1970s made for dancing.

clue.text: Beer enjoyed regularly initially could make you this?

definitions.text: Beer enjoyed regularly initially could make you this?

parts.note: stout is a dark beer

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Drinking beer often might make you fatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a definition: a regular beer habit makes you plumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual beer drinking tends to make people heavier, i.e. more corpulent.

clue.text: Watch old boy take the first tennis shot

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to serve is to start a point in tennis

explanation.surface: Watching a former pupil start a tennis rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Be important nobleman

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a European aristocrat, equivalent to an earl

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning to matter and as a noun for a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Company backing new casinos for social events

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the company abbreviation is read backwards
new signals the letters of casinos made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A firm funding newly opened casinos to host functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions are special gatherings or functions, i.e. social events.

clue.text: Old forbidding smell

parts.note: dour means stern and forbidding

explanation.surface: An ancient, off-putting stench.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is a scent or aroma, so it is a smell.

clue.text: Son put on elderly people's TV programmes

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above, so the son's letter comes first

parts.note: OAPs are old age pensioners

explanation.surface: A son switching on the pensioners' favourite television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP stands for old age pensioner, the British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaps are soap operas, serial dramas shown on television.

clue.text: This writer returns with energy after pub ban

indicators.note: after places the energy word following the pub
returns means the setter's pronoun goes back the other way

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a bar is a pub
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: The setter comes back with renewed vigour after being barred from the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade, so it is a ban.

clue.text: Farmer might go in this area of land over river

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A farmer might cross a stretch of land beyond the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer drives a tractor, a vehicle for pulling machinery, so this describes it by its user.

clue.text: Slight student captured in poster

indicators.note: captured in means the student's letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: a poster is one who posts something, a sender
L is for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A slightly built student appearing in a picture on a wall poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' suggests a printed placard, but here it is someone who posts a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and slender both describe a thin, delicate build.

clue.text: Justify book having new opening

indicators.note: a new opening means the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Defending a book that has been given a fresh first chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new letter; changing the first letter of RESERVE gives a word only with D.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, so one's conduct can justify or warrant it.
